tags.problem: children being treated as less than whole people
tags.evidence: Built a 33-year television practice rooted in treating children as whole people. Aired a full televised minute of silence so children could think about who loved them.

tags.problem: childhood loneliness and fear
tags.evidence: For 33 years personally replied to every child who wrote him with handwritten two-page letters naming the child's specific concern.

tags.problem: children labelled uneducable by institutions that never tried
tags.evidence: Worked with children from asylums labelled uneducable, designed tactile materials, and put them through standard Italian public school exams. They passed.

tags.problem: adults imposing their pace on children instead of watching
tags.evidence: Observed children choosing work over toys, repeating activities dozens of times, and policing their own order. Built entire method from watching rather than directing.

tags.problem: people trapped inside bodies the world assumes are empty
tags.evidence: Spent 49 years spelling the world into the hand of a deafblind person, starting from the premise that Helen Keller had a full mind waiting for language.

tags.problem: the isolation of disability when no one adapts to reach you
tags.evidence: Switched from formal curriculum to spelling words into Helen's palm whenever Helen reached for something, building 575 words in six months through patience.

tags.problem: children having no rights over their own lives
tags.evidence: Laid down three rights every child already possessed: the right of today, the right of the child over its own death, and the right of the child to be what it wants to be.

tags.problem: adults hitting children while treating it as normal
tags.evidence: Wrote that it was unthinkable to hit an adult casually yet considered normal to give a child a tap or stinging smack, returning to this in radio broadcasts for the rest of his life.

tags.problem: children facing the darkest moments of history alone
tags.evidence: Refused offers to escape the Warsaw Ghetto, reportedly saying 'You do not leave children at a time like this.' Walked with 192 orphans to the Umschlagplatz.

tags.problem: children being excluded from play by other children
tags.evidence: Introduced a single rule: any child who asks to join another child's play must be allowed to join. Wrote a 1992 book arguing for it.

tags.problem: adults remembering children as cartoons instead of people
tags.evidence: Left an audio recorder running in her classroom and transcribed tapes every evening, saying the method stopped her from remembering children the way adults usually do.

tags.problem: newborns being treated as blank slates with no individuality
tags.evidence: Built a 28-item scale to produce a behavioural portrait showing parents who their specific baby already was from birth.

tags.problem: parents missing the first months of their child's life because governments won't protect leave
tags.evidence: Spent years testifying before Congress arguing that the first months were a developmental window governments could not afford to ignore.

tags.problem: babies being handled like objects rather than participants
tags.evidence: Trained caregivers to announce each movement before making it, wait for the baby to participate, and handle the body slowly enough that the baby could predict what was coming.

tags.problem: orphaned children losing the chance to develop on their own terms
tags.evidence: Central design decision was that babies were not to be positioned. They were placed on their backs and allowed to find rolling, sitting, crawling and standing at their own pace.

tags.problem: the invisible damage of insecure attachment in early life
tags.evidence: Created the Strange Situation procedure to classify attachment patterns, converting attachment theory from clinical hypothesis into a measurable phenomenon.

tags.problem: nobody being able to measure something as slippery as a baby's trust
tags.evidence: Designed an eight-episode lab procedure to code infant behaviour across caregiver separations and reunions, identifying secure, avoidant and resistant patterns.

tags.problem: poor people dying of treatable diseases because the system decided they weren't worth treating
tags.evidence: Argued that the rural poor deserved the same treatment standards as patients at Harvard hospitals. Walked eight hours to reach one patient as a clinical standard.

tags.problem: global health policies sacrificing individuals for cost efficiency
tags.evidence: Fought the WHO's protocol that assumed first-line TB drugs would work, insisting second-line drugs had to be given even at higher cost to patients with drug-resistant TB.

tags.problem: newborns being called fine without anyone actually checking
tags.evidence: Scribbled five assessment categories on a napkin because too many newborns were being called fine without structured examination. The Apgar score became standard worldwide.

tags.problem: birth defects being ignored by medical research
tags.evidence: Became one of the first prominent voices on birth defects research at the March of Dimes, advocating for universal rubella vaccination during the 1964-65 pandemic.

tags.problem: people dying in pain because hospitals weren't designed for dying
tags.evidence: Introduced the concept of total pain and argued that opioid dosing had to be anticipatory rather than waiting for the patient to beg.

tags.problem: the medical system treating death as failure rather than a human experience
tags.evidence: Built St Christopher's Hospice to demonstrate that dying could be attended to with the same rigour as recovery, and died in her own hospice using the protocols she designed.

tags.problem: children being murdered for the crime of being born Jewish
tags.evidence: Helped smuggle Jewish children out of the Warsaw Ghetto and buried lists of their names in glass jars so families could be reunited after the war.

tags.problem: identities being erased along with lives
tags.evidence: Kept paper lists recording each child's original name, new name, and current hiding place, preserving identity through the worst attempt to destroy it.

tags.problem: ecological destruction intertwined with women's disempowerment
tags.evidence: The Nobel committee tied conservation, democracy and peace together, which was the argument Maathai had been making for 27 years: forest clearing and women's disempowerment were the same problem.

tags.problem: authoritarian suppression of civil society
tags.evidence: Was beaten unconscious at Uhuru Park, attacked at Karura Forest, and kept returning each time the Moi government tried to silence her.

tags.problem: people chasing winning instead of building character
tags.evidence: Built the Pyramid of Success around character traits, not basketball skills, and told players their career should read as a life first, a game second.

tags.problem: excellence being undermined by ignoring small details
tags.evidence: Demonstrated how to put on socks on the first day of practice each season, teaching that nothing at the elite level was beneath attention.

tags.problem: people unable to feel their place in the universe because nobody translated the scale for them
tags.evidence: Co-wrote and narrated Cosmos reaching 500 million viewers. Lobbied NASA to photograph Earth as a pale blue pixel from 6 billion kilometres away.

tags.problem: critical thinking being absent from public life
tags.evidence: Laid out the Baloney Detection Kit, nine heuristics for critical thinking, and taught a Cornell senior seminar on the same material.

tags.problem: people never seeing the natural world because nobody filmed it properly
tags.evidence: Created the template for blue-chip natural history documentaries, deliberately restricting his own screen time so the subjects could hold the frame.

tags.problem: ecological collapse happening while most people don't notice
tags.evidence: Since 2019 his documentaries have taken an explicit environmentalist stance, addressing COP26 at 95 about the terrible decline he witnessed in his lifetime.

tags.problem: absolute certainty turning humans into monsters
tags.evidence: Walked into the ash pond at Auschwitz and said: 'When people believe that they have absolute knowledge, with no test in reality, this is how they behave.'

tags.problem: specialisation letting scientists abandon moral responsibility for their work
tags.evidence: Refused to specialise, arguing that specialisation was the mechanism by which scientists surrendered their moral claims over their own work.

tags.problem: patients being reduced to diagnoses instead of seen as whole people
tags.evidence: Treated cases as portraits rather than diagnoses, refusing to reduce people to symptoms. His essay collection title was itself a case study.

tags.problem: neurological conditions stripping people of identity with no one noticing
tags.evidence: Documented post-encephalitic patients unable to move or speak for decades, then recorded their temporary returns to speech and recognition with levodopa.

tags.problem: Americans being afraid to cook because perfection felt required
tags.evidence: Kept mistakes in on live television so the viewer at home would believe they could do it too. Treated the fear as the enemy, not the roux.

tags.problem: French cooking being locked behind elitism and inaccessibility
tags.evidence: Deliberately over-detailed 726 pages so an American home cook with no French training could replicate any recipe in a normal kitchen.

tags.problem: positive liberty becoming the door through which tyrannies enter
tags.evidence: Argued that positive liberty, well-intentioned, had historically been the gateway for tyranny, drawing the distinction that structured most writing on freedom.

tags.problem: intellectual rigidity from seeing the world through only one organizing idea
tags.evidence: Divided thinkers into hedgehogs and foxes, claiming Tolstoy was a fox who wanted to be a hedgehog, valuing the many-perspectives approach.

tags.problem: scientific orthodoxy rejecting correct ideas because they came from the wrong person
tags.evidence: Had her paper rejected by roughly fifteen journals before publication. Twelve years later the genetic evidence proved her right about endosymbiosis.

tags.problem: the gravitational pull of a famous male partner on a young woman scientist
tags.evidence: Treated the Sagan years as a cautionary tale, saying she had to learn twice to hold her own ground, once in marriage and once in her field.

tags.problem: species being wiped out without anyone noticing or caring
tags.evidence: Proposed the Half-Earth idea: setting aside 50% of the planet's surface for other species to stop the sixth great extinction.

tags.problem: the gap between technical science and public understanding
tags.evidence: Won two Pulitzers including one for a 732-page technical encyclopedia, arguing the distinction between technical and popular writing was damaging to both sides.

tags.problem: people unable to recognize their own life story as meaningful
tags.evidence: Proposed the monomyth, a universal hero's journey pattern underlying all cultures' myths, giving people a framework to understand their own path.

tags.problem: confusing bliss with pleasure instead of vocation
tags.evidence: Sometimes wished he had said 'follow your blisters' instead of 'follow your bliss,' meaning the thing that was worth being hurt by.

tags.problem: illness being loaded with shame through metaphors like battle and invasion
tags.evidence: Wrote Illness as Metaphor during cancer treatment, arguing that metaphors damaged patients by loading their illness with moral meaning.

tags.problem: serious criticism being too afraid to engage with popular culture
tags.evidence: Notes on Camp took a sensibility unnamed outside gay subcultures and gave it critical treatment, reframing what a serious critic was allowed to take seriously.

tags.problem: watching suffering from a safe distance without being changed by it
tags.evidence: Flew into besieged Sarajevo to direct a play, saying she had not gone to document the siege but to be useful inside it.

tags.problem: Western thought treating other cultures as primitive rather than structurally complex
tags.evidence: Spent decades showing that myths from the Amazon through Central America to the Arctic followed transformation grids as rigorous as any Western system.

tags.problem: the human mind being assumed to work differently in different cultures
tags.evidence: Spent decades mapping myth-complexes across continents, arguing that structural relations between elements were universal, not culturally contingent.

tags.problem: human origins being told as a simple story when the reality was far more tangled
tags.evidence: Discovered that modern humans interbred with Neanderthals and found the Denisovans from a single finger bone, rewriting standard accounts of human origins.

tags.problem: ancient DNA being too contaminated for anyone to trust the results
tags.evidence: His main technical obsession for three decades was contamination, pioneering clean room protocols so that anyone could believe the results.

tags.problem: cities being destroyed by planners who never walked the streets they designed
tags.evidence: Attacked the entire mid-century consensus of urban renewal from her apartment, naming phenomena like 'eyes on the street' and 'sidewalk ballet.'

tags.problem: powerful institutions bulldozing communities that have no voice
tags.evidence: Led the fight that defeated Robert Moses's ten-lane expressway through Lower Manhattan, the first time Moses had ever lost a highway fight.

tags.problem: movements dying when their charismatic leader is removed
tags.evidence: Argued that a leader-centred organisation could be decapitated by assassination or scandal. Her most quoted line: 'Strong people don't need strong leaders.'

tags.problem: local people being overlooked by visiting celebrity organisers
tags.evidence: Built NAACP branches by listening for who was already trusted on the ground and building around that person rather than a visiting organiser.

tags.problem: Black women being erased from the movements they helped build
tags.evidence: Was a core organiser of the 1963 March on Washington but was not invited to speak. No Black woman was. She objected in writing and kept objecting for decades.

tags.problem: women doing the institutional work while men take the microphones
tags.evidence: Ran the NCNW for 32 years providing infrastructure behind many initiatives credited to male-led organisations.

tags.problem: gay people being forced out of the movements they built
tags.evidence: Was pushed out of the SCLC to protect King after Adam Clayton Powell threatened to float a false rumour of an affair. He kept organising in harder-to-see roles.

tags.problem: nonviolence being misunderstood as passivity rather than a strategic discipline
tags.evidence: Argued King into removing the gun and sending guards away during the Montgomery boycott, reframing it as a nonviolent action rather than defensive.

tags.problem: Black people being systematically prevented from voting
tags.evidence: Was failed on the literacy test, fired for attempting to register, retook the test twice, then had to pay two years of poll tax before she could actually vote.

tags.problem: poor Black women having their bodies violated by the state without consent
tags.evidence: Coined 'Mississippi appendectomy' to describe forced sterilisation of poor Black women under cover of other procedures, after her own uninformed hysterectomy.

tags.problem: voting rights being meaningless if people still cannot eat
tags.evidence: Founded Freedom Farm Cooperative with a pig bank, concluding that voting rights alone weren't enough if Black families in Sunflower County still could not eat.

tags.problem: communities being abandoned by everyone who could leave
tags.evidence: Refused to relocate from Detroit for 62 years, saying you could not organise a place you did not live in.

tags.problem: young people in declining cities being treated as problems rather than repair crews
tags.evidence: Founded Detroit Summer at 77, mobilising young people to plant gardens and rehabilitate buildings instead of treating them as a population to be managed.

tags.problem: ordinary people having no power against institutions that control their lives
tags.evidence: Built the modern template for community organising rooted in institutions people already belonged to, like parishes and unions, not abstract movements.

tags.problem: communities being too fragmented to fight back against exploitation
tags.evidence: Organised the Back of the Yards neighbourhood by bringing together Polish, Lithuanian, Slovak, Mexican and African American residents through their existing institutions.

tags.problem: citizens being forced to perform lies they no longer believe
tags.evidence: Described post-totalitarianism as a condition where citizens were forced to 'live within a lie,' using the example of a greengrocer displaying a sign from fear, not conviction.

tags.problem: individual creative expression being criminalized by the state
tags.evidence: Co-wrote Charter 77 in direct response to the prosecution of the Plastic People of the Universe for their underground music.

tags.problem: people being owned as property
tags.evidence: Escaped slavery and returned to the South roughly 13 times to guide approximately 70 enslaved people to freedom. There is no record of her ever losing a passenger.

tags.problem: the elderly having nowhere to be cared for with dignity
tags.evidence: Founded the Harriet Tubman Home for the Aged and eventually moved into it herself as a resident.

tags.problem: an entire race being enslaved while the country celebrated freedom
tags.evidence: Delivered 'What to the Slave is the Fourth of July?' identifying the holiday as a mockery from the standpoint of the enslaved.

tags.problem: Black people being assumed incapable of eloquence or intelligence
tags.evidence: Wrote his Narrative partly because Northern audiences had started to disbelieve that a man who spoke so well could actually have been enslaved.

tags.problem: poor immigrants having no access to the resources that could change their lives
tags.evidence: Opened Hull House with activities from night school to art gallery to bathhouse, making a single door lead to any of it for 2,000 visitors a week.

tags.problem: charity from a distance not working because it never gets close enough
tags.evidence: Argued that the volunteer had to move in to the neighbourhood she was trying to change, a principle she lived by for 46 years.

tags.problem: homeless people being asked to prove they deserve help
tags.evidence: Houses of Hospitality offered food and shelter without intake forms, conditions or proselytising. Staff lived alongside the people they served.

tags.problem: poverty and war being treated as separate issues from faith
tags.evidence: Combined radical pacifism, Catholic social teaching and direct hospitality for the homeless for nearly 50 years.

tags.problem: ordinary people's stories being erased from their own country's history
tags.evidence: Turned cab drivers, waitresses and steelworkers into the authors of America's history through oral histories like Working and Hard Times.

tags.problem: work being stripped of meaning and reduced to a paycheck
tags.evidence: His thesis in Working was that work is 'about a search for daily meaning as well as daily bread,' interviewing people at almost every job an American could hold.

tags.problem: neglected tropical diseases killing people nobody powerful cared about
tags.evidence: Personally followed the Guinea worm programme for decades, reducing cases from 3.5 million to 14 by visiting affected villages into his 90s.

tags.problem: elections being stolen while the world looks away
tags.evidence: Observed 115 elections in 40 countries, publishing frank reports including on elections inside the United States.

tags.problem: the post-presidency being wasted on ceremony instead of service
tags.evidence: Founded the Carter Center and spent 44 years on disease eradication, election monitoring, and Habitat house-building.

tags.problem: an entire population being dehumanized by law based on skin colour
tags.evidence: Spent decades confronting apartheid, from writing warnings to the Prime Minister to chairing the Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

tags.problem: countries torn apart by violence having no way to process the truth without more violence
tags.evidence: Insisted TRC hearings include testimony from both sides, with amnesty conditional on full disclosure, creating a template exported to Rwanda and Colombia.

tags.problem: women's bodies being controlled and mutilated in the name of tradition
tags.evidence: Her 1972 book Women and Sex confronted female circumcision and domestic violence using clinical, first-person prose from her rural medical practice.

tags.problem: women being punished for speaking about what is done to them
tags.evidence: Lost three positions in one year for one book. Was imprisoned for publishing a feminist magazine. Used eyebrow pencil on toilet paper to keep writing.

tags.problem: Black stories being absent from the literary canon they helped build
tags.evidence: As senior editor at Random House she acquired Muhammad Ali, Angela Davis, and The Black Book, while writing novels that finished the canon with the other hand.

tags.problem: the horror of slavery being too abstract for modern readers to feel
tags.evidence: Found the true story of Margaret Garner in The Black Book project, an enslaved woman who killed her daughter rather than let her be returned. That fragment became Beloved.

tags.problem: private racial humiliation that white America refuses to acknowledge
tags.evidence: Translated private humiliation into public argument, debating Buckley at Cambridge on how the American Dream was achieved at the expense of the American Negro.

tags.problem: the distance between the powerful and the people they claim to represent
tags.evidence: Organised a meeting with Robert Kennedy that ended badly, treating it as proof that the distance between the administration and the movement was factual, not rhetorical.

tags.problem: political violence pressuring artists to become propagandists
tags.evidence: Held the line of 'silence-breaking rather than rabble-rousing' across four decades of the Troubles, refusing to let his poems be read as IRA anthems.

tags.problem: having your identity claimed by a country that is not yours
tags.evidence: Published a verse reply when included without permission in a British poetry anthology: 'My passport's green. No glass of ours was ever raised / To toast The Queen.'

tags.problem: an entire people being stateless and having no words recognized by the world
tags.evidence: Read 'Identity Card' aloud and was placed under house arrest for it. Drafted the Palestinian Declaration of Independence in literary Arabic.

tags.problem: exile being treated as a one-time event when it repeats with every return
tags.evidence: Was allowed to return on a four-day permit after 20+ years to bury a friend, writing about exile afterwards as a repeating act rather than a single event.

tags.problem: people being forced to hide parts of their identity to be accepted
tags.evidence: Published her self-description 'Black, lesbian, feminist, socialist, mother, warrior, poet' repeatedly, refusing to be listed in a narrower set of identities.

tags.problem: the feminist movement excluding women of colour
tags.evidence: Delivered 'The Master's Tools' speech criticising conference organisers for including only two women of colour, and co-founded Kitchen Table: Women of Color Press.

tags.problem: cancer patients being silenced into performing recovery
tags.evidence: Refused the prosthesis after mastectomy and published The Cancer Journals, arguing that cosmetic performance of recovery served hospitals more than patients.

tags.problem: Black talent being rejected by institutions that claim to value merit
tags.evidence: Applied to Curtis Institute in 1950 and was rejected. She believed it was racial. Curtis sent an honorary degree two days before her death in 2003.

tags.problem: Black children being murdered and the country expecting silence
tags.evidence: Wrote Mississippi Goddam in less than an hour after the Birmingham church bombing killed four Black girls, saying it ended her commercial career and began her political one.

tags.problem: military dictatorships silencing artists who give people a voice
tags.evidence: Was arrested on stage mid-performance in 1979 along with her entire audience. Forced into exile for three years.

tags.problem: a continent needing songs it can sing together when it cannot agree on anything else
tags.evidence: Performed Gracias a la Vida at nearly every concert for 38 years, becoming the voice of Latin American solidarity.

tags.problem: military governments crushing dissent with violence and no accountability
tags.evidence: Released Zombie mocking the army. 1,000 soldiers raided his compound, beat him severely, and threw his mother from a window. He delivered her coffin to the military headquarters.

tags.problem: artists being forced to choose between commercial access and honest expression
tags.evidence: Made tracks 15-30 minutes long deliberately to be unplayable on commercial radio, forcing distribution through live performance he could control.

tags.problem: speaking truth to power costing you your country
tags.evidence: Testified at the UN asking for an arms embargo on South Africa. The government revoked her citizenship, leaving her stateless for nearly 30 years.

tags.problem: a woman losing everything for who she marries
tags.evidence: After marrying Stokely Carmichael, her US concerts were cancelled, recording contract dropped, and visa refused. The cost of one marriage was almost her entire American career.

tags.problem: childhood trauma stealing a person's voice
tags.evidence: Was mute for nearly five years after being raped at age eight. A family friend coaxed her out of silence by asking her to read poetry aloud.

tags.problem: Black women's stories being absent from American literature
tags.evidence: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings was one of the first widely read memoirs by a Black woman in America, returning to the bestseller list 24 years after publication.

tags.problem: a body in constant pain with no way to express what that feels like
tags.evidence: A bus accident at 18 broke her spine in three places and her right leg in eleven. She painted from a mirror above her hospital bed for the rest of her life.

tags.problem: women artists being read through sexual lenses they never chose
tags.evidence: Rejected the sexual reading of her flower paintings for fifty years, saying 'they're really talking about their own affairs.'

tags.problem: the world not being ready for what a woman artist already knows
tags.evidence: Produced the first fully abstract paintings in Western art around 1906, years before Kandinsky, then specified they not be shown until 20 years after her death.

tags.problem: female creative work being dismissed by male authorities
tags.evidence: Showed her Temple paintings to Rudolf Steiner in 1908. He was critical, telling her contemporaries wouldn't understand. She stopped abstract work for four years.

tags.problem: childhood betrayal living inside the body for decades with no outlet
tags.evidence: Revealed publicly at age 70 that her childhood governess had been her father's mistress and that her sculpture imagery was wholly autobiographical.

tags.problem: women artists being ignored until they are old enough to be safe
tags.evidence: Her first major retrospective at MoMA came at age 70 after forty years of making sculpture as a peripheral figure. Her most ambitious project arrived in her ninth decade.

tags.problem: artistic vision being constrained by commercial timidity
tags.evidence: Shot Seven Samurai for 148 days at three times budget, refusing to cut the rain battle scene. Studio had to wait on weather and dump hundreds of tons of water.

tags.problem: grief too deep to speak about directly
tags.evidence: Did not write about his brother's suicide until fifty years later, titling the chapter 'A Story I Don't Want to Tell.' The silence itself was the form.

tags.problem: Latin American reality being too extraordinary for European literary categories
tags.evidence: Argued in his Nobel lecture that the extraordinary history of Latin America was already unrealistic and that European literary categories were the narrow ones.

tags.problem: governments silencing journalists who expose the truth
tags.evidence: His 1955 shipwreck investigation contradicted the government's version of events. The government shut down the paper.

tags.problem: women artists being defined by male interpretations of their work
tags.evidence: Rejected the sexual reading of her flower paintings for fifty years, repeating the correction in essentially identical language across four decades of interviews.

tags.problem: losing the ability to create and refusing to accept it
tags.evidence: Lost most of her central vision at 84 but did not stop working, turning to clay and painting with assistants for fourteen more years.

tags.problem: African people being reduced to props in Western psychological dramas
tags.evidence: Argued that Conrad was 'a bloody racist' and Heart of Darkness reduced Africans to props. The lecture became a founding text of postcolonial literary criticism.

tags.problem: an entire continent's literary voice needing a vehicle to be heard
tags.evidence: Things Fall Apart introduced English that could carry Igbo proverbs without footnotes, establishing the publishing infrastructure for Africa's literary canon.

tags.problem: having an interior life that no existing literary form can hold
tags.evidence: Published her first novel at 23 with a voice that had no clear precedent in Brazilian fiction, interior and non-linear.

tags.problem: the body betraying the writer's instrument
tags.evidence: Nearly lost her writing hand in a fire in 1966. Continued to write afterwards with the damaged hand.

tags.problem: sacred architecture taking longer than a human lifetime to complete
tags.evidence: Devoted his final decade exclusively to the Sagrada Familia, living on the building site and begging door to door for stonemason wages.

tags.problem: conventional mathematics being too limited for organic structural form
tags.evidence: Built inverted scale models using weighted strings to calculate structural loads, bypassing mathematics and producing shapes no ruler-and-compass method would have generated.

tags.problem: design treating different media as separate problems instead of one
tags.evidence: Treated a chair, a house, and a film about the universe as the same design problem, working across furniture, film, exhibition and architecture.

tags.problem: good design being too expensive for ordinary people
tags.evidence: Assembled their home from off-the-shelf industrial steel components ordered from a catalogue, and the Lounge Chair was designed as a one-off gift.

tags.problem: gardens being designed without understanding colour as a sequence in time
tags.evidence: Treated the herbaceous border as a sequence of colour moving from silver-grey through hot reds and back, studying Turner and Impressionist colour theory.

tags.problem: rural crafts and knowledge vanishing without being recorded
tags.evidence: Published Old West Surrey photographing and sketching vanishing wheelwrights, ironwork, and cottage interiors before they disappeared.

tags.problem: Black Americans being denied their own identity and self-determination
tags.evidence: Delivered The Ballot or the Bullet laying out the stark choice: work within the electoral system or defend themselves with arms.

tags.problem: racial hatred being taught as religious truth
tags.evidence: After making Hajj he publicly repudiated twelve years of preaching racial separation, saying it was not supported by Islam as he now understood it.

tags.problem: an entire nation being ruled by a foreign power through everyday compliance
tags.evidence: Developed satyagraha as mass nonviolent resistance, from the Salt March to daily spinning as concrete boycott of British textile imports.

tags.problem: exploitative contracts that rob peasants of their livelihood
tags.evidence: Stayed for months in Champaran interviewing thousands of peasants forced by British indigo planters under exploitative contracts, submitting statements to a commission.

tags.problem: women's exploitation being hidden behind glamour
tags.evidence: Went undercover as a Playboy Bunny and exposed the exploitative working conditions, invasive medical exams, and low pay.

tags.problem: women having no mass-market voice of their own
tags.evidence: Co-founded Ms. magazine when there was no mass-market feminist periodical in the US. The test issue sold out in eight days.

tags.problem: women being absent from political office at every level
tags.evidence: Co-founded the National Women's Political Caucus to push women into office with training, funding, and endorsements. Roughly a quarter of women who served in Congress passed through its pipeline.

tags.problem: farmworkers being exploited with no legal protection or representation
tags.evidence: Co-founded the NFWA and led the Delano grape strike that secured the first significant contracts for agricultural workers in US history.

tags.problem: the temptation of violence destroying a movement from within
tags.evidence: Fasted for 25 days as a response to growing pressure to use violent tactics, subordinating his own body to hold the nonviolent line.

tags.problem: the physical world containing forces nobody had yet isolated or measured
tags.evidence: Processed a tonne of pitchblende in a leaking shed to yield one tenth of a gram of radium, doing heavy industrial work disguised as chemistry.

tags.problem: wounded soldiers dying because field hospitals lacked basic diagnostic tools
tags.evidence: Directed installation of 20 mobile X-ray vehicles and 200+ field units in WWI, personally driving some vans and training 150 women as operators.

tags.problem: women scientists having their work used without permission or credit
tags.evidence: Her colleague showed Photograph 51 to Watson without her permission. Watson and Crick produced their model weeks later. Her papers were published as supporting confirmation.

tags.problem: rigorous pattern extraction taking so long that others publish first
tags.evidence: Was working carefully through competing A form data before publishing the B form results. Watson and Crick completed their model the day after her papers arrived.

tags.problem: a scientific discovery being ignored for 35 years because the field wasn't ready
tags.evidence: Discovered transposable genetic elements in 1948. The field responded with puzzlement and hostility. She won the Nobel in 1983, 35 years later.

tags.problem: research depending on patience and sensory attention in a system that rewards speed
tags.evidence: Her method was hours in the maize field, waiting for patterns to declare themselves. She called it 'a feeling for the organism.'

tags.problem: Black women's mathematical brilliance being invisible inside segregated institutions
tags.evidence: Worked in a segregated computing section at NACA. Her transfer is one of the first documented cases of a Black woman mathematician being poached from a segregated pool.

tags.problem: machines replacing human judgment before anyone checks the machines
tags.evidence: John Glenn refused to fly until Katherine Johnson had checked the computer's orbital trajectory calculations by hand.

tags.problem: humanity defining itself by what separates it from animals rather than what connects it
tags.evidence: Observed chimpanzees making tools, ending the working definition of Homo sapiens as 'the tool-using animal.'

tags.problem: species collapsing from habitat destruction while the people who study them stay in the field
tags.evidence: Decided in 1986 she could no longer continue as a field researcher while the chimpanzee population was collapsing. Began 300 days of travel a year for advocacy.

tags.problem: industrial chemicals poisoning the natural world while governments look away
tags.evidence: Published Silent Spring exposing DDT bioaccumulation the chemical industry had been hiding since the 1940s. Wrote it while dying of cancer she kept secret.

tags.problem: scientific truth being attacked by corporate interests
tags.evidence: The chemical industry responded with legal threats. She kept her cancer diagnosis secret so her credibility could not be attacked on grounds of illness.

tags.problem: humans managing land without understanding they are part of it
tags.evidence: Shot a wolf and watched the fierce green fire die in her eyes, then spent the rest of his life rebuilding his profession around the concept of 'thinking like a mountain.'

tags.problem: wilderness having no legal protection
tags.evidence: His 1921 paper led to the first formal wilderness designation in the US federal system, setting precedent for the Wilderness Act of 1964.

tags.problem: state violence against civilians being hidden because journalists are too afraid to report it
tags.evidence: Reported on the Second Chechen War for seven years, travelling alone into villages Russian forces had swept, interviewing civilians. Was assassinated on Putin's birthday.

tags.problem: truth-tellers being murdered to maintain silence
tags.evidence: Warned 'People sometimes pay with their lives for saying aloud what they think.' Was shot dead in her elevator ten months later.

tags.problem: meaninglessness as the central human suffering
tags.evidence: Founded logotherapy defining the search for meaning as the primary human motivation, specifying three ways meaning could be realised including through unavoidable suffering.

tags.problem: people unable to find purpose after extreme trauma
tags.evidence: Lost his wife, brother, and mother in the camps. Chose to remain in Vienna, resume practice, and rebuild, applying his own theory of choosing attitude toward unchangeable facts.

tags.problem: a superpower having no strategic framework for understanding its main adversary
